children: Shares of Insilico Medicine rose Tuesday after a new study showed the company's experimental drug meant to treat an age-related lung disease could have antiaging properties.
The stock gained as much as 9.9% to 52.40 Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to US$6.68, before paring gains to last trade 8.2% higher.

The tech-bio company, which uses artificial intelligence to discover and develop drugs, said the preliminary study for the drug candidate, known as rentosertib, was published in a peer-reviewed journal using Phase 2a trial data.
Citi analysts said the findings validate Insilico's aging-biology-led discovery approach. The study is also viewed as a further differentiator for its lead asset, it added.
"We see meaningful upside to InSilico's platform visibility and pipeline optionality," the Citi analysts said in a note.
However, Citi said the findings remain exploratory, based on a small dataset, and don't demonstrate lifespan extension or represent a registrational endpoint.

Success in future trials would give support to the AI-driven model that Insilico and other biotech firms are pioneering. While the study's results appear promising, confirmation of rentosertib's age-reversing potential requires further investigation, said InSilico Co-Chief Executive Alex Zhavoronkov in an interview.

title: Insilico Shares Rise After Study Shows Experimental Drug's Antiaging Potential
